title: IP addresses, subnets and ping
summary: Two PCs on one wire cannot talk. Read their addresses, work out why, and fix it.

tasks.title: Read an address
tasks.text: Open a shell on **pc1** and look at its network interface `eth0`. What is its IPv4 address, written with its prefix (like `192.168.0.5/24`)?
hints: `ip -br addr` prints one line per interface.
Ignore `lo`, the loopback interface. You want the `eth0` line.

solution.note: The address is `10.11.1.10` and the prefix `/24` says the first 24 bits (`10.11.1`) name the network.

answer_cmd.cmd: ip -br addr show dev eth0 | awk '{print $3}'

tasks.title: Subnet arithmetic
tasks.text: A `/26` network leaves 6 bits for hosts. How many **usable** host addresses does it have?
hints: 6 host bits give 2^6 = 64 addresses in total.
Two of them are reserved: the network address (all host bits 0) and the broadcast address (all host bits 1).

solution.note: 2^6 = 64 addresses, minus the network and broadcast addresses, leaves **62**.

tasks.title: Find the fault
tasks.text: From pc1, `ping -c 2 10.11.1.20` (pc2's intended address) fails. Open a shell on **pc2** and read its address. Which network address does pc2 currently think it lives in? (Answer like `192.168.0.0`.)
hints: The network address is the address with all host bits set to zero. For a `/24`, that means the last number becomes 0.

solution.note: pc2 has `10.11.9.20/24`, so it believes its network is `10.11.9.0/24`. pc1 is in `10.11.1.0/24`. Different networks, and no router between them, so neither will even try to deliver directly.

tasks.title: Fix pc2
tasks.text: Give **pc2** the address `10.11.1.20/24` (and remove the wrong one) so that pc1 can ping it.
hints: Addresses are managed with `ip addr add <address>/<prefix> dev <interface>` and `ip addr del ...`.
On pc2: `ip addr del 10.11.9.20/24 dev eth0`, then `ip addr add 10.11.1.20/24 dev eth0`.

steps.cmd: ip addr flush dev eth0 && ip addr add 10.11.1.20/24 dev eth0

tasks.title: Meet ARP
tasks.text: IP packets on a local network are delivered to hardware (MAC) addresses. After a successful ping, pc1 has learned pc2's MAC address. What is it?
hints: pc1 keeps what it learned in its neighbour (ARP) table.
On pc1: `ip neigh`. Look for the line starting with `10.11.1.20`; the MAC follows `lladdr`.
